Introduction
This document provides essential information on the components of the Biodiversity & Land Use Key
Issue to enable users of ESG Ratings to understand how MSCI Sustainability & Climate’s (MSCI S&C’s)
outputs are determined. Biodiversity & Land Use is a Key Issue in the Environmental Pillar of the MSCI
ESG Ratings model. MSCI S&C evaluates companies on the potential impact of their operations on
biodiversity in their areas of operation and their efforts to manage the environmental impact of their
operations.
For additional details on the MSCI ESG Ratings Model, refer to the Data, ratings and scores section of
“ESG Ratings Methodology.”

Risks associated with this Key Issue
• Loss of formal and social license to operate.
• Litigation by landowners and other affected parties.
• Increased costs of land protection and reclamation.

The definitions of the data points in each component are given below:
Biodiversity & Land Use Policy & Disclosure score
The Biodiversity & Land Use Policy & Disclosure score evaluates the company’s disclosure of
biodiversity and land use policies, including commitments to habitat restoration, minimizing disturbances,
engagement with external stakeholders or standard to address the biodiversity impacts of operations. it
is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong initiatives.
• Involvement with external stakeholder groups to address the biodiversity impacts of its
operations
Definition: Indicates whether there are external stakeholder groups that work with the company to
address the biodiversity impacts of its operations.

• Scope of third-party engagement or standard to address the biodiversity impacts of
operations
Definition: The estimated share of operations with ecosystem protection programs certified or assured
by an external stakeholder group.
• Commitment to minimize disturbances on biodiversity
Definition: Indicates whether the company has disclosed an explicit commitment to minimize
disturbances on biodiversity, for example following the mitigation hierarchy of “avoid, minimize, restore
and offset.”
• Commitment to reclaim habitat on disturbed land
Definition: Indicates whether the company has disclosed an explicit policy to eventually reclaim the
habitat of all disturbed land.
• Scope of biodiversity and land reclamation policy
Definition: The scope of operations covered by the company’s disclosed biodiversity and land
reclamation policy, where applicable (i.e., all operations including its supply chain, all direct operations, or
partial operations).
Biodiversity & Land Use Programs & Structures score
The Biodiversity & Land Programs & Structures score evaluates the company’s ability to manage
biodiversity impacts through structured programs and practices, including ecosystem protection
initiatives and biodiversity impact assessments for new operations. it is expressed as a 0–10 score,
where 10 indicates strong initiatives.
• Extent of programs to protect ecosystems
Definition: Assesses the comprehensiveness of the company’s steps to protect ecosystems, for
example, whether the company creates ecosystem reserves vs. isolated initiatives to protect single
species, and whether such practices apply to all major sites or only selected operations.
• Conducts biodiversity impact assessments
Definition: Indicates whether the company conducts biodiversity impact assessments prior to settling in
new areas.

Biodiversity & Land Use Performance score
The Biodiversity & Land Use Performance score evaluates the company's performance on biodiversity &
land use metrics (oil spill intensity) relative to its peers. It is expressed as a 0-10 score, with 10 indicating
strong performance.
• Oil spills performance relative to peers
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on oil spills intensity (normalized by sales), and trend
in oil spills intensity, relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates the highest level
of performance.
o Oil spill intensity industry relative score
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on oil spill intensity metrics (total volume
of oil spilled normalized by sales) relative to its industry peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score,
where 10 indicates strong performance.
 Three-year average oil spill intensity (sales based)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average oil spill intensity,
calculated as total oil spill volume per unit of sales.
o Oil spill intensity industry relative trend score
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on the three-year trend in oil spill
intensity (year-over-year change in oil spill volume normalized by sales) relative to its
industry peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.
 Three-year average year-over-year oil spill intensity trend (sales based)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year trend in oil spill intensity.
Controversies
A controversy deduction ranging from 0 to 5 points is subtracted from the overall Management score
based on the severity, status, and the company’s role in the controversies facing the company on this
Key Issue. The result is the Management score. The following categories of controversies are used in the
assessment:
• Biodiversity & land use controversies.
• Oil spills.
• Toxic releases to water/land controversies.
For more details on how controversies are included in the MSCI ESG Ratings model, refer to Section:
Controversies cases, of “ESG Ratings Methodology.”

The Biodiversity Business Impacts score of a business activity is assessed by examining the business
impacts that are present for that activity. Nine business impacts arising from biodiversity and ecosystem
changes are considered such as disruption of operations, restricted access to land and resources and
litigation. For each business activity, each impact is presented as a 0 or 1 value, with 1 indicating that the
impact is present. The number of impacts that apply to each activity is counted and scaled to a factor of
10 to calculate the Biodiversity Business Impacts score.

The Controversies score of a business activity is determined by the percentage of companies involved in
a biodiversity controversy assessed as Moderate to Very Severe among all the companies with the same
primary business activity. Refer to Section: Controversies cases, of “ESG Ratings Methodology” for
details on how the severity of controversy cases is assessed.
